mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary conditions, which increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth is below 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rates indicate a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when UNRATE is below 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates strong economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when INDPRO is rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both federal funds rates and unemployment rates rise simultaneously, it indicates tightening monetary conditions and labor market constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE increases by 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when both FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weakening demand in the housing market, which reduces related industries' performance and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when HOUST growth is negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation erodes profit margins and increases uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 35% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows but employment remains high, it indicates inefficiency in resource allocation, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate < 2% YoY and PAYEMS growth rate > 0%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 45% of periods when GDPC1 growth is slow but PAYEMS growth is positive, the hypothesis is rejected.
